claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology is a collaboration between the Center for Open Science and Science Exchange that seeks to address concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology (RP:CB) is a collaboration between the Center for Open Science and Science Exchange that seeks to address concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Errington et al., 2014, which establishes the nature and purpose of the RP:CB project.

claim: Castellarin et al. reported in 2012 that overall abundance of Fusobacterium nucleatum RNA was increased by approximately 79 fold in colorectal carcinoma as compared to adjacent normal biopsies, as determined by RNA sequencing.
source: In 2012, Castellarin et al. reported that overall abundance of Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum) RNA was increased by approximately 79 fold in colorectal carcinoma (CRC) as compared to adjacent normal biopsies, as determined by RNA sequencing.
evidence: This claim references findings from Castellarin et al. 2012, providing specific quantitative data about F. nucleatum RNA abundance.

claim: Castellarin et al. measured F. nucleatum DNA abundance in 99 CRC and adjacent normal tissue biopsies from a patient cohort and found that the presence of F. nucleatum DNA was 415 times greater in CRC tissue than adjacent normal tissue.
source: Next, they measured F. nucleatum DNA abundance in 99 CRC and adjacent normal tissue biopsies from a patient cohort and found that the presence of F. nucleatum DNA was 415 times greater in CRC tissue than adjacent normal tissue.
evidence: This claim references specific quantitative findings from the Castellarin et al. study regarding DNA abundance measurements.
